name: Udaipur
tagline: The lake city of marble palaces and Aravalli hills.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Oct, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: Come October to March for cool, lake-full days; time it to the World Music Festival in February or Mewar Festival in spring, and avoid the searing April-to-June heat.

ourTake.lede: Time everything around water and light, a sunset boat on Lake Pichola, breakfast on a terrace facing the City Palace, an evening when the palaces are floodlit and reflected. Two full days is enough for the city itself; use a third for a slow drive to Kumbhalgarh fort or the Ranakpur Jain temples. Avoid the monsoon-fed crowds around Diwali if you want the ghats to yourself, and always ask for a lake-facing room, the difference is the entire visit.
ourTake.comeIf: You want lake palaces and India's most romantic hotels without leaving the country.
ourTake.skipIf: You want a beach, nightlife or cool mountain air.

items.name: Bujera Fort
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler, Udaipur luxury hotels list (2024, recommended)
items.description: A small, personally-run fort-house of real character, with the lakes and Monsoon Palace laid out below.

items.name: City Palace of Udaipur
items.description: The living seat of the Mewar dynasty, the oldest ruling family in the world, rising in tiers of balconies and mirror-work above Lake Pichola. Come early with a palace historian; the private royal apartments and the Zenana Mahal reward a slow, unhurried morning far more than a rushed group tour.

items.name: Crystal Gallery
items.description: Maharana Sajjan Singh's untouched 1877 order of Birmingham crystal, so vast it was never fully unpacked in his lifetime, including crystal chairs, tables, fountains and even a jewelled bed. A hushed, one-of-a-kind room that rewards the collector's eye; pair it with a look down into the gilded Durbar Hall.

items.name: Sunset boat ride on Lake Pichola
items.description: The essential Udaipur hour: a boat gliding past the Taj Lake Palace and the ghats as the Aravallis turn rose and gold behind them. A privately chartered boat from the City Palace jetty at golden hour, arranged through your hotel, turns a shared cruise into your own royal romance on the water.

items.name: Jag Mandir island palace
items.description: The 17th-century island pleasure-palace of black-and-white marble that sheltered Prince Khurram, later Shah Jahan, and is said to have inspired the Taj Mahal. Step off the boat for a candle-lit dinner under the domed Gul Mahal, a favourite setting for intimate royal-style celebrations and proposals.

items.name: Taj Lake Palace
items.description: The white-marble palace that seems to float on Lake Pichola, built by Maharana Jagat Singh II and now one of the most romantic hotels on earth, reached only by the hotel's own boat. Even non-residents can arrange a lunch or high tea by boat; for a stay, it is the definitive multi-generational Udaipur address.

items.name: Jagdish Temple
items.description: A soaring 1651 Indo-Aryan temple to Lord Vishnu, carved with elephants and musicians and alive with aarti bells a short walk from the palace gate. Slip in for the morning or evening aarti; the temple sits at the head of the old-city lanes, so it makes the natural start to a heritage walk.

items.name: Sajjangarh (Monsoon Palace) at sunset
items.description: The white hilltop palace built to watch the monsoon clouds roll in, now the finest sunset perch in Udaipur, with all three lakes and the old city laid out below. Time the drive up for late afternoon; a private car and a picnic from your hotel make the golden hour genuinely memorable.

items.name: Bagore ki Haveli & the Dharohar dance show
items.description: A restored 18th-century noble's haveli on the Pichola waterfront whose evening Dharohar show is the best folk performance in Rajasthan, ending with a dancer balancing eleven brass pots on her head. Book the front row; the courtyard setting under lamplight is intimate and family-friendly across generations.

items.name: Fateh Sagar Lake & Nehru Garden
items.description: The city's second great lake, ringed by the Aravallis, with a little island garden reached by boat and a breezy promenade that locals stroll at dusk. A gentle counterpoint to the palace crowds; the lakeside cafes and the sunset light make it an easy, unhurried outing for families.

items.name: Saheliyon ki Bari
items.description: The Garden of the Maidens, laid out by Maharana Sangram Singh for the royal ladies, with lotus pools, marble elephants and fountains that run on nothing but gravity from the lake above. A cool, shaded, thoroughly photogenic hour; children love the elephant fountains that switch on for visitors.

items.name: Ambrai Ghat
items.area: Hanuman Ghat, west bank of Lake Pichola
items.description: The single best face-on view of the City Palace and Lake Palace, especially when both light up at night and mirror in the water. Come for a sundowner at the ghat-side terrace; it is the postcard of Udaipur and the reason the west bank is worth crossing to.

items.name: Gangaur Ghat
items.description: The most atmospheric of Pichola's stepped ghats, framed by the triple-arched Tripolia gateway and busiest during the spring Gangaur festival, when the lake fills with lamp-lit processions. Wander down at dawn to watch the old city wake by the water before the day's boats set out.

items.name: Bada Bazaar & the old city lanes
items.description: The warren of lanes between Jagdish Temple and Clock Tower, where generations of families still sell silver, block-printed textiles, bangles and Mewari miniatures from tiny shophouses. Best explored on foot with a guide who knows the genuine ateliers; a discreet private tailor or silversmith visit can be arranged.

items.name: Miniature painting workshop
items.description: Udaipur is the living heart of the Mewar school of miniature painting, and the old-city ateliers still work in squirrel-hair brushes and stone-ground pigments as they did for the Maharanas. A private session with a master painter, watching a peacock or a Krishna scene emerge on marble or old paper, is a quietly extraordinary keepsake.

items.name: Vintage & Classic Car Collection
items.description: The Mewar royal garage, with the 1934 Rolls-Royce Phantom and Cadillac convertibles that carried Maharanas and Queen Elizabeth II, kept in the original 1930s state motor house. A short, delightful stop for car lovers and multi-gen families; several of the cars still run for palace weddings.

items.name: Shilpgram crafts village
items.area: West of Fateh Sagar, near Havala village
items.description: A living rural-arts complex where potters, weavers, puppeteers and painters from across western India work in recreated village huts, most vivid during the winter Shilpgram Utsav. A relaxed way to meet artisans and buy at the source; a good half-day for families with children.

items.name: Ahar cenotaphs & museum
items.area: Ahar, 2 km east of the city
items.description: A serene field of some nineteen royal cenotaphs where the Maharanas of Mewar were cremated, beside a small museum holding pottery and a rare 10th-century Buddha and finds dating back nearly four thousand years. Almost always empty, it is a soulful, contemplative counterweight to the palaces.

items.name: Karni Mata ropeway to Machla Magra
items.description: A short cable-car glide up Machla Magra hill to the Karni Mata temple, delivering a sweeping bird's-eye of Lake Pichola, the City Palace and the old city at your feet. Ride up near sunset; it pairs neatly with the Doodh Talai gardens and musical fountain below.

items.name: Doodh Talai musical fountain & gardens
items.area: Doodh Talai, south of the old city
items.description: A pretty lakelet at the foot of the ropeway hill, with rock gardens, a sunset point and an evening musical fountain that draws local families. An easy, low-key evening stroll with lake views; combine it with the ropeway for a gentle end to the day.

items.name: Neemach Mata hike
items.description: A steepish climb up Dewali hill to a hilltop temple to the royal household goddess, rewarded with one of the widest, least-crowded panoramas of Fateh Sagar and the city. Go at first light for the cool and the birdlife; a genuinely local, active alternative to the driving circuit.

items.name: Badi Lake (Bari ka Talab)
items.area: Badi village, ~12 km from the city
items.description: A serene, offbeat lake built by Maharana Raj Singh I after a famine, with clean marble ghats and hills all around and far fewer visitors than the city lakes. A favourite quiet-escape picnic spot; beautiful in the monsoon when the overflow spills over the stone weirs.

items.name: Sukhadia Circle
items.description: A grand three-tiered marble fountain on a landscaped roundabout that comes alive in the evening with illuminated water and a lively food market of chaat, faluda and street snacks. A cheerful, unpretentious evening for families; the veg street food is plentiful and easy for Jain diners.

items.name: Gulab Bagh (Sajjan Niwas Garden)
items.area: Between City Palace and Lake Pichola
items.description: Udaipur's largest garden, a hundred-acre Victorian-era rose park laid out by Maharana Sajjan Singh, with a heritage library, lotus ponds and shaded avenues in the heart of the old city. A calm green lung for a morning walk; the toy train pleases younger children.

items.name: Heritage walk of the old city
items.description: A guided morning weave through the lanes from Jagdish Temple past painted havelis, silversmiths, temple courtyards and hidden Pichola viewpoints that you would never find alone. The best single introduction to Udaipur's texture; the top hotels arrange private historian-led walks tailored to your interests.

items.name: Kumbhalgarh Fort
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Kumbhalgarh Fort, part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan
items.description: The mighty 15th-century mountain fortress of Rana Kumbha, wrapped in a defensive wall over 36 km long, second only to the Great Wall of China, birthplace of the legendary Maharana Pratap. Time the visit for the late-afternoon light on the ramparts and stay for the sound-and-light show; combine with Ranakpur in one grand day.

items.name: Ranakpur Jain temples
items.description: A 15th-century marble masterpiece to the Tirthankara Adinatha, its 1,444 pillars each carved differently so no two are alike, set in a quiet forested valley. Deeply serene and naturally Jain-reverent; usually paired with Kumbhalgarh, it is worth lingering over the marble at an unhurried pace.

items.name: Chittorgarh Fort
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Chittorgarh Fort, part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan
items.description: The largest fort in India and the emotional heart of Rajput valour, its towers of victory and fame rising over the scene of three legendary sieges and the jauhar of Rani Padmini. A powerful, story-laden full day; a good guide brings the Vijay Stambh and Padmini's palace to life.

items.name: Nathdwara, Shrinathji Temple
items.description: The most revered Krishna shrine of the Pushtimarg tradition, where the seven-year-old Shrinathji is dressed and worshipped through eight daily darshans amid the town's famous Pichwai painters. A meaningful pilgrimage half-day; the giant hand-painted Pichwai cloths make it a magnet for collectors.

items.name: Eklingji Temple complex
items.description: The ancestral temple of Lord Shiva as ruling deity of Mewar, a complex of some 108 shrines in white marble and black stone where the Maharana still worships as the god's regent. Atmospheric and devout; go for the evening aarti and pair with Nagda next door.

items.name: Nagda, Sas-Bahu temples
items.area: Day trip, ~23 km north, near Eklingji
items.description: A pair of exquisitely carved 10th-century Vishnu temples beside a lake, their intricate stonework among the oldest and finest in the region, a short hop from Eklingji. A tranquil, uncrowded stop for lovers of ancient temple architecture; easily folded into the Eklingji-Nathdwara circuit.

items.name: Jaisamand Lake (Dhebar Lake)
items.description: One of Asia's largest artificial lakes, dammed in 1685 by Maharana Jai Singh, with marble cenotaphs, summer palaces and islands, and a wildlife sanctuary on its hilly shores. A wide, wild-feeling escape from the city bustle; boating and birdlife make it a rewarding leisurely day.

items.name: Menar bird village
items.description: A community-protected 'bird village' whose lakes host thousands of migratory birds each winter, from flamingos to cranes, watched over by villagers who guard rather than hunt them. A soulful dawn outing for birders and photographers; best from November to February.

items.name: The Oberoi Udaivilas grounds
items.area: Haridasji ki Magri, west bank of Lake Pichola
items.description: A palace-hotel of gilded domes, reflecting pools and its own stretch of Pichola shoreline, consistently rated among the world's finest resorts and set within a wildlife-rich former royal hunting reserve. Even for non-residents, a private boat arrival for lunch or spa is a serene indulgence; for a stay it is Udaipur luxury at its peak.

items.name: Sunset at Ambrai / Lake Pichola dinner cruise
items.description: As the palaces light up, a slow private boat with a Mewari thali or a chef's tasting on board turns dinner into the definitive Udaipur evening. Easily arranged through heritage hotels, with veg and Jain menus as the effortless default; a favourite for anniversaries and quiet family celebrations.

items.name: Rajasthani cooking class
items.description: Learn dal-baati-churma, gatte ki sabzi and Mewari sweets from a home cook in an old-city haveli kitchen, often ending with a rooftop meal over the lake. Naturally vegetarian and Jain-adaptable, it is a warm, hands-on way for families to take a taste of Udaipur home.

items.name: Miniature-painting shopping at the source
items.description: Beyond a workshop, the serious Mewar-miniature galleries near Jagdish Temple sell museum-grade work on old paper, silk and marble, some by nationally recognised master families. A discreet, guided visit lets collectors commission or acquire genuine pieces rather than tourist reproductions.

items.name: Silver & textile shopping in the old city
items.description: Udaipur's lanes are a treasury of tribal silver, bandhani and block-printed textiles, and Rajasthani jootis, sold by families who have traded here for generations. A knowledgeable guide steers you to the authentic ateliers; bespoke tailoring and private silver appointments can be set up through your hotel.

items.name: Vintage-car heritage drive
items.description: The royal household still runs some of its vintage Rolls-Royces and Cadillacs for special occasions, and a chauffeured heritage-car drive to a palace dinner is a signature Mewar flourish. A memorable touch for weddings and milestone celebrations, arranged through the palace's own hospitality group.

items.name: Vidhya Niwas / rooftop lake-view sundowners
items.description: The old-city rooftops on Lal Ghat and Hanuman Ghat look straight across Pichola to the palaces, and a sundowner up top is the local way to end a day of walking. Choose a quiet heritage rooftop rather than the crowded cafes for the calmest, most cinematic view.

items.name: Haldighati battlefield & Maharana Pratap memorial
items.area: Day trip, ~40 km north, near Nathdwara
items.description: The narrow mountain pass where Maharana Pratap and his beloved horse Chetak fought the Mughals in 1576, now with a museum and memorial that tell the Mewar valour story vividly. A short, stirring add-on to the Eklingji-Nathdwara circuit, especially with children learning the legend.

items.name: Sunset point & rope-walk at Machla Magra
items.description: The landscaped sunset garden atop Machla Magra hill offers a calm, ticketed viewpoint over the lakes without the crowds of Sajjangarh. A quieter in-city sunset option that pairs perfectly with the Karni Mata ropeway ride up.

items.name: Bohra Ganesh Temple
items.description: A much-loved local Ganesh temple, one of the oldest in the city, thronged by students and families seeking blessings, especially before exams and new ventures. A gentle, genuinely local devotional stop away from the tourist trail, best in the morning.

items.name: Vintage boat to Mohan Mandir & Arsi Vilas
items.description: Beyond Jag Mandir, Pichola holds the small royal island pavilions of Mohan Mandir and the bird-rich Arsi Vilas islet, seen on a longer private boat loop. A quieter, connoisseur's angle on the lake for those who want more than the standard cruise.

items.name: Spa & wellness at a palace hotel
items.description: Udaipur's palace resorts offer some of India's finest spas, from Ayurvedic royal rituals to lake-view treatment pavilions and yoga at dawn over the water. A restorative anchor to a multi-generational stay, easily woven around the sightseeing days.

items.name: Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary trek
items.area: Day trip / overnight, Aravalli hills near Kumbhalgarh
items.description: The forested hills around the great fort protect leopards, wolves and sloth bears, with guided nature walks and jeep trails through wild Aravalli country. A rugged, active add-on for those extending the Kumbhalgarh day into an overnight in the hills.

items.name: Sheesh Mahal
credentials: Inside Taj Lake Palace, Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice Best of the Best 2025, No. 1 One-of-a-Kind Hotel globally
items.description: Royal Mewari fine dining inside the floating palace, the grandest dinner in the city, on the water.

items.name: Udai Kothi rooftop / Sheesh Mahal restaurants in-hotel
items.area: Lake Pichola (west bank, The Oberoi Udaivilas)
credentials: Inside The Oberoi Udaivilas, Travel + Leisure World's Best Awards 2024, Best Luxury Resort (Editor's Choice, India)
items.description: Considered Indian and European cooking in the most decorated hotel in Udaipur, flawless, and framed by the lake.

Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice
items.description: The lakeside table with the postcard view, the City Palace and Lake Palace lit up across the water.

items.name: Upré by 1559 AD
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India, featured Udaipur restaurant
Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice

credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India, featured Udaipur spot
Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice

items.name: Amrit Sagar Bar

credentials: Inside Taj Fateh Prakash Palace, Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Travel Awards 2024 (Taj Hotels honoured)

plan.heading: 3 days in Udaipur, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: The lake at its own pace

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Settle into the Taj Lake Palace or the Leela Palace, then take a private boat across Pichola to Jag Mandir before the light hardens.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Walk the City Palace with a curator, lingering in the Sheesh Mahal and the Zenana courtyards rather than rushing the full circuit.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sundowners on the Leela's lakefront terrace, then dinner at Sheesh Mahal at the Fateh Prakash overlooking the water.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A morning with a miniature painter in the old city, followed by the stepwells and the restored havelis around Bagore-ki-Haveli.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Drive out to the Jagdish Temple lanes for textiles, then rest through the afternoon heat by the pool.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A private thali dinner at Ambrai on the ghats, with the City Palace lit across the lake.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Early drive to the Jain temples at Ranakpur, timed for the marble before the crowds.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch and a slow return via Kumbhalgarh's fort walls, or a spa afternoon back at the hotel if you'd rather stay close.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A last dinner at Upre by 1559 AD on the rooftop, watching the boats settle for the night.

items.name: Lake Pichola waterfront (Gangaur Ghat)
items.description: The old-city ghats and heritage havelis right on the water, atmospheric and walkable, best for first-timers.

items.name: Lake Palace / island stays
items.description: The famous island hotels reached only by boat; for a cocooned, once-in-a-lifetime stay cut off from the town.

items.name: Fateh Sagar & the ridge
items.description: Quieter lake and hillside above the bustle, with space and views; suits those who want calm over old-city immediacy.

events.name: Mewar Festival
events.note: A spring festival tied to Gangaur, with a Lake Pichola boat procession and City Palace celebrations honouring the goddess.

events.name: Shilpgram Utsav
events.note: The big crafts-and-folk fair at the Shilpgram rural arts village, drawing artisans from across western India.

events.name: Udaipur World Music Festival
events.note: A weekend of international and Indian acts across lakeside and heritage stages in the City of Lakes.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay lakeside for the sunset views, the palace hotels on and around Lake Pichola are the reason to come. Dress is relaxed but cover shoulders and knees for the City Palace and Jagdish Temple, and shoes come off at temple thresholds.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Maharana Pratap Airport (UDR) at Dabok, roughly 40 minutes from the lake, and let a chauffeured car meet you airside; the Taj and Oberoi properties also arrange a private boat transfer across Lake Pichola for their island palaces.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car with driver for the town and its temples, and a hotel boat for the lake and the island palaces, the old city itself is best seen slowly on foot.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: 4G is reliable across the city and hotel wifi is strong; an Airtel or Jio eSIM loaded before arrival saves the paperwork of a local SIM.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee (INR); cards are accepted at hotels and better shops but keep cash for markets and boatmen, and tip around 10 percent or leave it to your hotel to settle.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: October to March is kind: cool, clear, the lakes full after the monsoon. Avoid April to June, when the Rajasthan heat climbs past 40C, and July to September, when the rains arrive.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi (approx 1h20m), Mumbai (approx 1h30m) and Bengaluru (approx 2h15m) into Maharana Pratap Airport (UDR); IndiGo and Air India run the routes, with SpiceJet on some. A small airport with a short indoor walk, so a car-to-door pickup matters more than a lounge; the hotels send one.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required beyond routine cover; carry the usual Hep A/typhoid boosters if not current. Very safe, calm city. Drink sealed or filtered water only, as everywhere in India.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Effortless for vegetarian and Jain travellers; Rajasthani cuisine is largely vegetarian and Jain (no onion/garlic) versions are understood everywhere. Ambrai and the hotel dining rooms at the Oberoi Udaivilas and Taj Lake Palace do refined vegetarian thalis.
